title: Mexican Revolution
summary: The Mexican Revolution is dated to about 1910-1920. It began with Francisco Madero's call to arms on 20 November 1910; Díaz resigned the presidency by the end of May 1911 after the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez. The Constitutionalists later took control, save Villa and Zapata's strongholds, and the 1917 Constitution expressed the revolution's goals, including limits on private property.

uncertainty.note: Start is the date Madero's call to arms was set to begin (6 p.m., 20 November 1910). End year 1920 is the Library of Congress's "approximately 1910-1920"; no opened page gives an end date.

where.historical_name: Mexico (Díaz presidency, then provisional and revolutionary governments); pin at Mexico City

importance.justification: The upheaval that ended the Díaz regime and produced the 1917 Constitution and land reform.

audience_note: This record concerns a decade of civil war that harmed many civilians; the sources opened give no death toll, and none is stated here.
